notes.title: New Agate Visual Novel Celestia: Chain of Fate is releasing 12th September!
notes.notes:
Greetings, Principals!

A new game from ‘Valthirian Arc: Hero School Story 2’ developer Agate is about to drop! [b]Celestia: Chain of Fate[/b] releases on September 12th, 2024 on Steam! Enter this fantasy-romance visual novel with a compelling narrative about Angelus, Daemons, and Half Bloods over 20 chapters and 23 alternate endings!

[b]Wishlist Now on Steam![/b]  https://store.steampowered.com/app/2791850/Celestia_Chain_of_Fate/

[previewyoutube=KvyrI407-60;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]About the Game:[/b]
The perfect life you’ve known as a daughter of a Duke is about to change forever. With the revelation of your new hybrid identity, as a descendant of Angelus and Daemon, you must learn to live in a new world.

Uncover the secrets of your family history and learn to control the magical abilities you hold. Along the way, you'll have the chance to develop relationships with one of three romanceable characters, each with their own unique traits and personalities.

It’s down to you to hold your friendships and advance your love interests while also prioritising your education. Remember not to neglect your studies as you'll need to overcome a series of challenges to graduate!

notes.title: UPDATE[12A]//Hotfix Patch 1.0.1
notes.notes:
Greetings, Principals

We hope you’re enjoying the game! Have you assembled the perfect party to complete those challenging quests? Or are you still fine-tuning your strategy through trial and error? Regardless of where you stand, we’re thrilled to have you on board with us on this adventure and hope you find endless enjoyment in our game.

We understand some players have encountered issues when playing the game, but don’t worry! Our dedicated development team has been hard at work addressing these issues. We’re excited to bring you this latest update, which includes the following fixes:

- Remove unused Arcsilo blueprint as a research requirement.
- Fixed rare occurrence issues where students spawned in the wrong dungeon.
- Fixed behavior on some enemies.
- Fixed visual effects on some student skills that don’t work properly during battle.
- Fixed changes on settings that aren’t properly saved.
- Fixed alignment issues on party selection.
- Fixed issue where required student can be removed from the party and cause the game to crash.
- Fixed camera setting on exploration.
- Fixed achievements that players can’t complete.
- Fixed the HUD issue that sometimes doesn’t appear during battle.
- Fixed issues where players can’t complete quests.
- Fixed issues where students get stuck in some areas inside the dungeon.
- Fixed audio volume issue.
- Fixed the issue where the game crashes during exploration when the enemy chases the party.
- Fixed the issue where Rodno wasn’t removed from the academy after his graduation.
- Fixed issue in snowman minigame where the displayed button prompt is not correct.
- Fixed cinematic graduation bug where the principal is glitching.
- Fixed localization issues.
- Fixed issue when a battle with three monsters will make the player drop from the ground.
- Fixed some issues in fishing minigame.

That’s all for this update, Principals! If you find other issues, don't hesitate to report them. We are committed to delivering an even smoother and more enjoyable gaming experience. Thank you for being part of our community, and stay tuned for more exciting updates in the future!

notes.title: Update [11]//Patch 0.12.0.0
notes.notes:
We’ve got other students coming, Principals. And one of them is not even a human! 

Meet Zero Four and Kayla Palmer. Zero Four is a sentient arcstone-powered automaton built to replace heroes. Despite their slender physique, Zero Four can beat all monsters in Valthiria, even those who create trouble for professional heroes. However, without an official hero license, Zero Four can’t become a professional hero. To obtain the necessary license, they have come to your academy. 

The mastermind behind this remarkable creation is Kayla Palmer, a young inventor from Chernov. After her past tragedy, she has dedicated her life to designing machines capable of replacing heroes. She comes to your academy to witness Zero Four's triumph over fellow students and become the best hero Valthiria has ever seen. 

See their action in this video! 

[previewyoutube=bEnYkKT6cK0;full][/previewyoutube]

Being a hero involves more than just defeating monsters. So, can you help them understand that while they are attending the academy? 

Not only robots, but there will also be pets too! Yup, in this update, there will be pets that will spawn in the school grounds and those animals will change for every season. We hope their cuteness brings more fun to the academy.

notes.title: Update [7]//Patch 0.8.0.0 and Console Announcement
notes.notes:
Hi Principals! We are back with another exciting update for you. 

[h1]Latest Update Ver 0.8.0.0[/h1]

Things are getting a little hotter in Valthiria—all thanks to a recently discovered Hidden Dungeon. 

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/c4d7e98ad4e57b2b80787609ac506675e40b5c46.png[/img]

With glassy obsidian, rough pumice, and molten lava all around, this hidden dungeon might be too hot to handle, except for the future heroes from the Academy. Just remind your students: “don’t play with fire”! 

With the discovery of the fiery dungeon, it became clearer that Valthiria is not entirely free of danger. Monsters show up now and then, deterring the residents of Valthiria from solo travel. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/7da9ffad785a0ff48b267284ed4beab3283f81b5.png[/img]

To help ease the residents of Valthiria, the Academy offers a solution: Escort Mission! With students as bodyguard-slash-companion, travelers could be safe from various monsters that lurks in the forest. And maybe from a loneliness, too. No judgement. 

Be careful though, as every traveler will take a space on your team. Some might be able to help in fight, while some can’t. It’s part of the mission: fighting with less attack power and more possible casualties! Can your students handle the challenge? 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/7845c615b734fc2107411379f175452f2bc31622.png[/img]

At least it would be a great networking event!

notes.title: Update [6]//Patch 0.7.0.0
notes.notes:
Greetings, Principals, and...Lady Principals!

One of the most-awaited updates, we’re excited to announce that the female principal is finally ready to join the Academy! We recognize that having this choice is an important thing for our players, so we hope this option will enhance your playing experience even more. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/c36efcf3760e68c6c6eb8d64799c89181e2f49af.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/8b56600493b34a944ade5274319430c731a7fcd5.png[/img]

Ever heard about “strike the first blow”? Now in battle, delivering the first strike will give you an advantage! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/ce15592c27061479fac559de4e2d572ff5890910.png[/img]

Every time you manage to strike an enemy first, another student in the party will immediately dish out a second attack, giving you a notable head start in the battle. You can maximize this advantage by finding the right formation for your party. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/b09a2bb08909512a53073ed11c989e2de5cccd4a.png[/img]

And last buat not least: the principal isn’t the only new character in this update. We also added two new champions. Meet: Tiana Cherenkov and Chad Donnervogel!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/031786126cf7ae6f172091b2376d0176f67a68ff.png[/img]

They have different outlooks on life, and they are eager to prove each other wrong. If you see them around the Academy, they’re most likely competing in something. Something that you didn’t even know could be a competition. At least it’s free entertainment, right?

One student said that Tiana and Chad have hundreds of these minor competitions, and their total wins are almost always at a draw. Another student says that even the teachers are split on who will be the winner in the end. Catch their friendly (or not?) rivalry on the upcoming update!

[h3]This update includes:[/h3]
•	New feature: Female Principal
•	New feature: Pre-emptive attacks
•	Added in-game Achievements
•	Major UI overhaul
•	Added sorting feature on several UIs
•	Improved skill visuals
•	New characters: Chad & Tiana
•	More quests, tasks, and events
•	Balanced Champion skills and enemy difficulty
•	Added student spawn animation
•	Fixed a fatal error when pressing [ESC] after choosing a student in battle
•	Fixed graduation and enrollment that keep popping up when cutscenes are in play

[h3]Known Issue:[/h3]
If your monitor is not capable of 2560 x 1440 resolution, please do not set your resolution to 2560 x 1440 in the game settings, as doing so will result in a bug where your cursor movement will be limited.
If the bug does occur, press Alt + Enter to enter windowed mode, then change the resolution via the game settings to a resolution supported by your monitor.

notes.title: Dev Diary #16: Exploration System Update
notes.notes:
Greetings, Principals!

It’s been quite a while, isn’t it? To tell you the truth, we’ve been hard at work improving all aspects of the game, one of them being the major change to our exploration system. We moved away from automatic exploration in our previous build to a more open one where you can freely explore the different areas in the game!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/6ff1770ae3e2e611f2b2466222bc250f2a121ff4.png[/img]

At present, there are 3 different areas in the world that you can explore in the early access with 3 more coming along the way  . These areas can be accessed through the world map, representing the varying biomes in the realm of Valthiria itself. Separated based on the combat difficulty, the explorable areas are:

1.	Plains – Difficulty: Easy
2.	Forest – Difficulty: Medium
3.	Mountain – Difficulty: Medium
4.	Desert – Difficulty: Hard (1st update)
5.	Tundra – Difficulty: Hard (2nd update)  
6.	Secret Area (3rd and final update)

Aside from giving players a more pronounced sense of agency, the change also brings about a slew of new features to improve the sense of progression in the exploration itself.

The first is the introduction of the Teleport Gate. In order to start exploring an area, you have to activate a dormant gate. After you activate it, you can fast travel directly to any gate you have activated  . Here’s a neat feature: If you (or your students) are itching to go home, you can directly teleport to the gate located in the academy as well!

Don’t rely on the Teleport Gate to take you away every time you’re in a bind though. There will be certain times when the gate won’t be active, such as when you’re being overrun by a gauntlet of monsters during a quest, or when you need to find an item in an area before you can proceed to the next one.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/ea1aab71ddf9f68e3d1c3a596b818dffcb3f830c.jpg[/img]

It’s not going to be very fun exploring large areas without a place to fall back to and rest, right? We’ve also added the campsite feature in our current build, where your students can lay down, relax, and enjoy the night sky from the comfort of their camp.

Your students may also choose to fully restore their HP at the camp, but there’s a caveat: the monsters they’ve defeated will respawn as well, so choose wisely when to rest and when to keep on adventuring!
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/6ae907e74b7961bb29ae24d4a7f6c0fb02d85045.png[/img]

We also know that you might have a little too much fun exploring to only stumble on areas where your students are underleveled. You don’t want to lose your dear students in an “accident,” wouldn’t you? That is why we also put blockades towards certain areas of the game. 

The blockade exists for a variety of reasons, but we ultimately put it so that you will have a far more focused experience while playing the game. This is how the blockade looks like in our current build, but we are working to make it blend more seamlessly to the areas that you are currently exploring:
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/924677c4a3d6ab5b1695809ce97ee43c6640a809.jpg[/img]

Well, that’s it for the update on the exploration mode! We’re looking forward to seeing you explore the different biomes that are populated with dangerous (and sometimes cute) monsters that we have lovingly crafted. Stay tuned for more information, we’ll see you on the next Dev Diary!

notes.title: Dev Diary #15: Dungeons Galore!
notes.notes:
Greetings, Principals!

Adventure awaits you in Valthiria, mostly in the deep dungeons scattered around the nation. Today we’ll be taking a deeper look into the dungeons and what secret lie within them. Each dungeon is segmented into regions and have their own distinct environment, monsters, rewards and quests. Currently there are the following 7 dungeon regions in-game:

1.	Plains 
2.	Desert
3.	Forest
4.	Mountains
5.	Tundra
6.	Swamp
7.	Cave

Your students will start off only having access to the plain areas first, but as the story and your academy progress new dungeons will be available for you to explore. Locked dungeons won’t be revealed until you have fulfilled the necessary conditions tied to the event system and exploration mechanic.    Selecting a dungeon will reveal its name and lore along with related quest and tasks available. The dungeon map itself will be revealed as you explore the place overtime.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/1098cf4f1bd748a161f09c8fc3688d32eeb73528.png[/img]

After selecting a dungeon, you need to choose your exploration party. An exploration party needs to consist of 4 students, no more, no less. Principals can assign which active skill to bring for each student with a maximum of 3 skills each. Choose wisely depending on the monster’s proficiency! You can see the monster proficiency list when selecting your dungeon. Some dungeons have monsters with every kind of proficiency, but some have no physical or have difficult combinations of particular proficiencies. 

Each dungeon terrain is unique, which you can probably imagine how the landscapes will be from each area’s name. A nice change of surroundings and potential terrain challenges for you to discover, best be prepared!

Well, that’s all about dungeons for now. Thanks for reading and we’ll see you in the next one, Principals!

Greetings, Principals!

With Halloween right around the corner, it’s only fitting that we let our monsters shine for the festivities. Here’s a closer look at the monsters you’ll encounter while exploring the dungeons of Valthiria.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/63d9597a01e25d6bc65550c48b412634578ecf94.jpg[/img]

We already mentioned before that monsters in Valthiria have evolved into having their own proficiencies, but did you know they also have their own archetypes? Currently we categorized monsters into 3 types based on their difficulty with 6 archetypes based on their attacks.  This of course can change in the future as we further develop the game. For the monster types themselves, there’s fodder, specialist and bosses. Fodder is the normal enemies you’ll encounter to gain experience. Specialists have a specific way to be defeated, but you can still try and brute force them down if you like. Bosses on the other hand are designed for you to get creative and strike them down, they will require a bit of pattern studying to defeat though. Now onto the archetypes!

[b]•	Normal[/b]
First off there’s your average joe monsters. You’ll probably be beating up these guys a lot. They have no specialties and are quite easy to kill. Slimes, balloons, you’ll probably encounter a lot of those during your early quests.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/43bad53710ae527e0fc2c880a656c59db06277a8.png[/img]

[b]•	Rusher[/b]
Rushers are the easier types of specialist you’ll encounter. They may be fast, but their attacks are relatively weak and only targets a single character. They do however have moderate HP and defense, so shield-breaking is key to winning this battle quickly. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/d168fd5932fdaf9f5532a46a569a0d13c8fddd4d.jpg[/img]

[b]•	Brute[/b]
Brute enemies may be slow but they hit hard, coupled with tremendous HP and defense. You will need to shield-break them and be wary of your hp when facing these enemies in your quests. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/c96b9589cec3235bfdbbe640774a59532c6b6fc3.png[/img]

[b]•	Horde [/b]
As you can probably guess by the name, hordes come in groups. Alone they’re pretty weak, but together they can be overwhelming. Hordes will always consist of low-level fodder type monsters, so they should be easy to handle if you can get the hang of weeding them out that is.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/22b8526a8871051c679af0e904b5e72cd34c3b3e.jpg[/img]

[b]•	Bomber[/b]
Bombers are mid-range enemies that can self-destruct, damaging your students in the process. Run or kill them ASAP because they will hurt if you don’t give it your all. You can tell a bomber is about to go off by their change in color.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/c5640c7045c7c3aa297f5d08f8cd0452a4d45f5c.png[/img]

[b]•	Healer[/b]
Again, a very on the nose name, these mid-range enemies have the ability to heal their friends. They do not possess any combat abilities, but they may increase difficulty in certain fights.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/2b6f3f32ef2be5af56a21f662e8e84e19e544711.jpg[/img]

Those are the monster types of Valthiria, careful not to bump into them on the streets this Halloween. Hope you all have a fun holiday and we’ll see you in the next one Principals!

notes.title: Dev Diary #12: World Building/Lore
notes.notes:
Greetings, Principal!

Previously we’ve talked a lot about features and game mechanics, but this time we’ll be talking more about the world of Valthiria itself. 

Taking place hundreds of years after the prequel in the northern parts of Valthiria, the nation have advanced to a whole new era. What once was a peaceful nation under one Queendom is now divided into 4 areas and factions, all because of the ancient powerful dragon, Fellwing. The Queendom may have persevered and slain the dragon, but not without sacrifice. The people discovered they have different hopes and dreams to rebuild their country and so, the four factions were formed.

Each faction has their own culture, proficiency affinity, and beliefs. Imagine it like the nations in Avatar : The Last Airbender if you will. Novoresk is the military-oriented domain which tries to protect the nation from northern dangers. Chernov is a scholarly domain, focusing more on researching the advancements of magic and bond with other factions. Perkuna is the most technologically advanced faction, creating various arc-devices for their people. Last but not least, there’s the Mokosil tribe, a mysterious self-sufficient faction focusing more on the divine proficiency.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/99c80b9e7eea472c58b2dd05164b90fe40c2db9d.png[/img]
 
‘Coincidentally’ your academy is right in the middle of these 4 factions, thus receiving students from all other areas while remaining under no one’s particular rule. Every student deserves a chance to be a hero for their nation, no matter where they came from. As the nation progress, so did the people and its enemies. Monsters evolved to have their own proficiencies, abilities to manipulate their body, nature or energy. These are more commonly known as the following four proficiencies; physical, magic, divine, and arcworks. 

Arcworks being the latest addition in the Valthirian Arc series. Technology escapes no one, even in the world of heroes. Long ago, Valthiria discovered a new element called the Arc Stone. Possessing an enormous amount of power and energy, these stone are now used to power up man-made machines called arc-devices. Arc-devices are used by everyone, extensively so by Arcsmiths who rely on arc-weapons in battle. These devices are so common that your academy has an Arc Tower holding up a massive arc-stone to power up all your students arc-devices.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/f6814dc98edc8a853e974a9914264dd6d0561812.png[/img]
 
As you progress through your academy, you’ll get to know all your students and faculty members. Getting involved in their stories, and discover issues not only in each area, but also a common threat, tipping the fragile balance of Valthiria. Of course, we’re not going to reveal to you what that threat is. You’ll just have to buy the game and experience the story for yourself!

Hope this helps you have a better understanding of Valthiria. If you’re still curious for more, check out our dev diary video series on Youtube.

notes.title: Dev Diary #11: Notifications
notes.notes:
Greetings, Principals!

If you recall in our 8th Dev Diary entry, we’ve talked about Principal Tasks and how it has helped testers get the hang of their duties and goals around the Academy. Well today, we’ll be talking about our updated notification system. 

Notifications, as you can guess, will notify Players about important events in the game and tasks that need immediate action. These notifications will appear in the Notification panel in the Academy HUD, some as temporary pop ups, while more pressing matters will be listed in the Notification List until resolved. Of course, you can still dismiss them altogether if it bothers you. Your academy, your rules.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/ce6c9c13f988ee9f219c55d915e05fd93f3800a9.png[/img]

When notifications are clicked, they will do an action based on the type of notification they are. There are 4 types of notification categorized based on their urgency levels:

1.	Important Notification
2.	Warning Notification
3.	Favorite Notification
4.	Normal Notification

Important notifications are mostly there to remind you about unscheduled students or event triggers. Warnings are about upcoming events and countdowns or about students getting kicked out of class. Normal notification tells you about student’s mood or performance, or just telling you about your achievements, and building lots. The daily life aspect of being a principal, if you will. Favorite notifications, are basically not that different from normal notifications, but it highlights your favorite students specifically. Because there’s always that angelic student that outshine the rest, isn’t there?

As you progress through your principal journey, more events will pop up. Most recent events will always be placed on top of the list. Important levels being prioritized first. Actions when notification are click depend on the nature of the notification itself. If it’s about students getting kicked out, then of course clicking the notification will direct you to the student schedule tab and mood. New building notifications when clicked, will open up the building list. Warning or event notifications will show you the calendar and things you have to prepare for that event.

These notifications serve not only as a reminder to help you manage your students, but also as shortcuts to streamline your job as principal. We want to make sure players enjoy their principal journey and not thinking the micro-managing aspect of this game as a chore. We’ll definitely keep improving those aspect as the game is being developed and we’re looking forward to your reception to our work.

That’s all for today’s Dev Diary, thanks as always for following along and we’ll see you in the next one, Principals!

notes.title: Dev Diary #10: Quest Exploration
notes.notes:
Greetings, Principals!

How was your week? Did you work hard? We sure did! Last week we talked about our playtest recap and here are some changes we’ve made based on tester’s feedback and our own experience with the game.

We present to you, the new and improved exploration system! Potentially at least, it’s still in the works, but we’ve done a lot to improve the exploration aspect of the game and we wanted to know what you guys think about it. For those who aren’t aware, VA:HSS2’s current build uses Auto Mode. Auto Mode means that students explore the dungeons automatically through a pre-coded route with no branching paths. Enemy encounters are unavoidable and your journey is pretty streamlined.

[previewyoutube=Qp9C-j39j3s;full][/previewyoutube]

It does the job and is good for busy principals who just want to lay back and watch their students kick some monster butt, but it could be better, right? That’s why we’ve been hard at work developing a more thorough exploration system, the Explore Mode. Explore Mode lets players take control of their party and roam around the quest areas themselves. This means bigger dungeons and more branching pathways, avoidable monster encounters, and more rewarding treasure hunts.

[previewyoutube=fs4Nev6M3Zc;full][/previewyoutube]

Basically, players get to free roam their quest areas, and find all the secrets in it (or not). Enemy encounters are now also in your control. It’s up to you whether you want to jump on your enemies, or simply sneak around to find all the treasures first. Do note that enemies might try to chase you though, you are in their territory afterall.

If you’re wondering why the change, well originally, we wanted principals to relax and let students move on their own while discovering new encounters along the way. Yet as we further worked on the game and new feedback kept coming in, we decided we should try exploration mechanics that provides more player agency. Hence, the Explore Mode was born!

We would like all of your feedback on this too. Principals play a big part in the development process and we would like to know your own preferences for the game. We will still keep the branching areas, more dynamic monster encounters, and treasure hunts. However, do you prefer exploring the areas yourselves, or letting the students roam on their own? Which sounds more appealing to you, Auto Mode or Explore mode?  Comment below and give us your feedback!

Your comments will help us decide which exploration mechanic works best for the game. And as the game development progress, we’ll be sure to add more exciting features that improve your overall gaming experience. 

That’s it for this week’s dev diary, please give us your feedback in the comments below. Don’t forget to wishlist us and we’ll see you in the next one, Principals!

notes.title: Dev Diary #9: 5th Playtest Recap
notes.notes:
Greetings, Principals!
Another playtest result has come in and today we’ll be showing you a recap of the feedback we received. A big thank you to all 75 testers who tried out our 5th alpha build. Your feedback is always appreciated and is crucial to the game’s development. Now let’s jump into the results.

1.	Time Allocation
As stated in our previous playtest recap, we hope to have a more balanced gameplay in VAHHS2. Our time allocation goal is a score of 5 to 6.5, which means testers have a balanced experience both in academy management and combat. In the 4th playtest testers rated the time allocation a 6.7, the current build has a score of 6.6 which still aligns well with our goal and we hope to maintain this score until release.

2.	Comparison with VA:HSS
About 30% of our 5th alpha play testers have played the first VA:HSS game. Out of that 30% about half preferred the previous hack and slash combat system compared to the current turn-based combat. However, the majority commends the game’s new academy management system, let it be the enrolling and graduation aspect or scheduling and courses. The story is also a noteworthy increase from the previous game.

3.	Changes from Previous Build	
We’ve implemented most academy management features in the 4th alpha. However, in the 5th alpha we also added some new features such as the student promotion system and principal task. The principal task as stated before, are goals and task for principals to complete and can help players accustom to the academy. Letting them fully experience all it has to offer. More than 70% of our testers found the principal task helpful and easy to understand, giving it a score of 7.15.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/98c141e753c7010c0bec49ad263a0f6d0001f3d0.png[/img]

Of course, we’re still further polishing the game so there are a few principal task bugs and issues here and there, but hopefully we’ll be able to get rid of those as the game gets closer upon release. One thing to note, we’ll probably add more principal task or clarification regarding student promotions. This is due to the fact that most testers quickly get the hand of scheduling and courses, however some testers completely missed the promotion feature.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/0649bde049f4ff0a2bdf10f0d41e36a1b67cb4ff.png[/img]

Another thing we plan to work on is the combat tutorial. The combat introduction was changed for the 5th playtest; however, this was met with mixed opinions as some felt the combat was clearer in the 4th alpha. A combat tutorial is currently planned in the works, so hopefully that will help players understand the overall gameplay. 

Buildings have also been improved, facilities are resized and have more varied models, the building upgrade layout have been modified as well, giving it a cleaner look. Building mood effects have also been updated to work properly with adjusted stats.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/7772dd99704f947c95e96a95afd30fa83aacb965.png[/img]

4.	UI/UX Update
One of the major updates in this build though is the UI. We added new nameplates for the students, new icons, updated the notification feature, implemented in-game menu on quests, updated skill descriptions, and many more. Notification being one of the major updated ones, with added notification for students kicked out of their classes and we also added a student list.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/08ebabf551b293005c64d5bf04dc3b628fb30296.png[/img]

The UI design gets a makeover as well, as you can see from the comparison above between the 4th and 5th alpha test. We made significant layout and background changes in the students tab. Courses description are updated, and the student stats are more organized. We’ll probably improve on the visual aesthetic of the UI next, also adding descriptions for some buttons as the game development progress. Recurring testers seem to appreciate the overall improved clarity, so that’s great news!

5.	Combat
Testers who have played the prequel have mixed feelings about the new combat system, some like it, some still preferred the hack and slash system from the first game. This is expected, as turn-based combat is not for everyone. However, testers appreciated the combat length not being too long or short, hitting that sweet spot. Quest time and exploration are considered a bit shorter than expected, but still well received. Skill execution and defense break are still the most favorable aspects of combat. However, we do realize we might need to add more skill chains, gimmicks, and of course, balancing the overall combat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/79f6a93d98f14235cc5846354b4cfad56a21b079.png[/img]

6.	Control
We improved the camera control making it more fluid and reactive, but we still want to improve on our camera speed and maybe add some camera invert options. Our feedback results also show that most of our testers use both keyboard and mouse control, although some messaged us that they actually prefer to use the controller. Something we were quite fascinated by and wonder about our audience. Are you a keyboard and mouse fan or more of a controller gamer? Let us know in the comments!

Overall progress is still going as planned. Some features were met less enthusiastically than we hoped, but nothing too far out of our expectations. We’re very glad that some returning players still like the game’s combat, despite the major change from the prequel. We’re also very appreciative of all the feedback we received, many of you made excellent suggestions and we hope we can implement some of them before release. If you have your own opinions and input for VA:HSS2 please feel free to tell us in the comments, or through our social media. 

That’s all for the 5th alpha playtest recap, don’t forget to wishlist us and we’ll see you in the next one, Principals!

notes.title: Dev Diary #7: Building Management
notes.notes:
Greetings, Principals!

Welcome to another entry of our beloved dev diary series. In today’s entry, it’s all about buildings. Like any other well-built academy, buildings are where students learn and sharpen their abilities.  In VAHSS2 however, buildings are a bit more specified in its types and usage. There are two types of buildings, classrooms and facilities. Classrooms are where you’ll be sending your students to on their monthly schedules. Students will gradually gain stats according to their attended classrooms. Facilities on the other hand, gives out passive stat gains to all active students without them needing to attend the facilities themselves. Convenient, huh?

Don’t think you can just place a bunch of facilities and rely on passive stat gains though, that would be too easy! Buildings are restricted to having no duplicates, so you can’t have 2 Gyms or 2 Infirmaries for example, you can only place one of each. But devs, what if there are too many students in one class?  Don’t worry, buildings don’t have any student limitations. You can assign all your students to one building and it wouldn’t cause any issues!

What you should be worried about is budgeting. Principals start off with a limited amount of gold at first, so try to plan accordingly. If you want to focus on a certain stat then prioritize buildings with relevant stat gains. Example, if you’re focusing on raising divine stats, then aim to build the Greenhouse and infirmary facility first. The Greenhouse adds 5 divine points per attendance while the infirmary gives a +1 divine stat per month with an additional of +10 HP during quests.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/e19baec864638bc26328a805264e8845ddfcc0b3.png[/img]

Besides raising stats, buildings can also influence students’ moods. Moods influence students’ academic performance, low moods reduce stat gains and can even get you kicked out of class! Higher moods on the other hand, will bring significantly better results. Most classes do cause a mood decrease, so we recommend placing a few mood boosting buildings, such as the Garden or Recreation Hall to optimize your students’ performance.

That covers the basics of buildings, now on to actually building and placing them! In VAHSS2, there’s a total of 14 build slots for you to build on. These slots are divided into three areas, the first area have 6 lots, while the 2nd area and 3rd have 4 build slots each. Principals start off in area 1 with only 6 build lots, other areas will open up as you progress and reach a certain level of prestige.

 Which slot you decide to place your building in and which order you place them won’t have any effect on stats, so go ahead and layout your academy as you like. Simply click on the building lot or you can go to the building list menu and choose your slot then select your desired building.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/27f984ef8258a8468578cba10f804bd25252f741.png[/img]

Easy, right? As your game progress, you should have enough money and resources to upgrade buildings. Upgrades will increase stat gains and help your students pass their courses faster. Each building can be upgraded up to 4 times. Each time the cost will increase, but so will the benefits. For example, the base price of the Mech Workshop is 1000 and has basic stats of +5 arc stat/attendance and –2 mood /attendance. The first upgrade costs 1500 and stats will increase to a + 10 arc stat/attendance and a - 3mood/attendance. These stat changes will linearly increase as the upgrades go on.

Most building upgrades are beneficial and result in fewer negative stats. Some however, do come at a cost, mainly the 4 main classrooms. Upgrading the Gym, Magic Arena, Mech Workshop, or Greenhouse will increase all of their stats, including the negative hit on your students’ mood. This of course is compensated by students completing their course requirements faster, but should be accommodated with other stat buffs to lessen its negative impact.

The best principals take account of both the academy’s efficiency and student happiness, and we’re sure you are all up to the challenge. We can’t wait to see your academy in its full glory. That’s all for this week’s dev diary. Thanks for tuning in, don’t forget to wishlist and we hope to see you in the next one, Principals!

notes.title: Dev Diary #6: School Management System
notes.notes:
Greetings, Principals! 

Welcome back to our Dev Diary series. Today we’re going to talk about the school management system and how we’ve improved from the prequel HSS game. As we’ve mentioned in our earlier dev diary, there are two common issues back in the first HSS game, mainly the slow real time progression and the fact that some principals love their students a bit too much, thus sending other students to graduate in their place instead.

In VAHSS2 we wanted our players to have less waiting time in the academy, so we decided to change up the time system. Instead of your usual hourly progression, time is now divided into blocks. Currently, one block is the equivalent of one in-game month. Time won’t progress into the next month unless the player commands it by clicking on the “End Month” button. This lets players plan out their student activities accordingly and simply skip time to the next month once they’re ready to progress.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/3a0c4fd3ede52c5c4a2a96072738d88cf68c12ac.png[/img]

Student graduation times have also changed. Back in the prequel, principals can send students off to graduate whenever the graduation pop-up appears, regardless of their academic performance. As we’ve mentioned before, this has been altered so that students will always graduate after 3 years. No need to worry about student shortage though, as each year a list of new potential students will arrive.  Out of a variety of enrolling students, principals get to select 3 students of their liking to teach and build into heroes. This creates a continues cycle of students entering and graduating the academy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/03de766f703d9687a7974e9028862f21877224de.png[/img]

In order to graduate well and receive better jobs, students will require high exam grades. In VAHSS2 exams are done twice a year, in which each year consist of 4 seasons and each season consists of 4 months. So, students will have a total of 8 months to prepare for their exam. Principals can help their students by assigning their courses and schedules each month. Each course has their own skill gain and academic points rewards. They are key to raising exam grades and getting promoted to different majors. In order to complete a course, students need to finish objectives such as completing quests and gaining certain stats. 

Stat gains can be done in various ways, but one of the main ways is by scheduling your students to learn in certain buildings such as the gym to raise their physical stats or the wizarding arena to gain magic stats. Some buildings also have passive stat gain effects, but we’ll explain more about that in a later date.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/e9fe5d6ba11b063af5f2d615017b2052de522f1f.png[/img]

That completes the stat gain issue, but what about quests? Well, at the end of each season, principals can send out 3 students to embark on a quest. A quest is all about honing your students’ combat skills and letting them off on an adventure to face various enemies. Be careful though, if your students’ party is wiped out, then they’d fail and have to retry on another season. However, if even only one party member survives, then the quest objective is completed and they’ll pass their course. Remember, each student only has 3 years to graduate, and it’s your job to prepare them to the best of your abilities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/63d9597a01e25d6bc65550c48b412634578ecf94.jpg[/img]

That’s it for the new school management system. We hope that these changes will encourage principals to take care of all their students, instead of just favoring that one godly built overachiever. A good principal should prepare their older students for graduation, while also not abandoning the teachings of their younger, less-experienced, students.

It may be a lot of hard work, but in the end it’s all worth it to see your once naïve students graduate into powerful heroes. Thanks for tuning in and hope to see you in the next dev diary, principals!

notes.title: Dev Diary #5: 4th Playtest Recap
notes.notes:
Greetings, Principals!

We’d like to do something a bit different today and show you our previous playtest results. Over 70 principals have joined the 4th Alpha test, and their opinions have greatly helped us further improve VAHSS2’s development. Here’s a recap of their input and our modifications so far:

1.	More Balanced Gameplay

One of our goals in VAHHS2 is to have a more balanced and academy-oriented gameplay compared to the previous game’s more combat heavy one. Out of our scoring system of 1, signifying combat-oriented gameplay, and 10, a more academy-oriented gameplay, testers rated the current build a 6.76. This aligns with our scoring goal of 5 to 6.5, and is a large improvement compared to the 3rd playtest that had a more combat-oriented score of 2.71.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/b932ceb6763794a93d1de6dc9fd580c92fa8bc27.png[/img]

2.	Academy Features Update

On our 4th alpha we wanted to test out more on the academy side, such as assigning the students schedules and courses to help them grow, a promotion system to promote your students, and the building upgrade feature to improve your academy. 

Some of these features have been showcased in the first and second alpha build but were incomplete or not functioning as we’d hope. In the 4th alpha we managed to fully implement all the academy gameplay features along with updating its UI.

Overall, the academy features were met with favorable reviews. Many testers stated it rounds up the system from the previous game and gives a more realistic and polished gameplay. 
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/d42bd562335f30a2893009b70ad153ef2c9d4d22.png[/img]

3.	Combat System Refinement

Testers favor the combat’s shield break feature, a feature that we’ve discussed in our previous dev diary. Many complimented that matching the student’s proficiency with the shield breaks adds an extra challenge to the game. However, the overall combat score still only has an average of 7, needing further balancing. We’ve also been improving the combat’s visuals effects, polished out some battle transitions, added indicators to better communicate enemy stats, and balance out the battle pacing.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/9a77573480594dce287094c4dc3cfed67adfb7bf.png[/img]

4.	Academy Layout Improvements

Along with the 4th alpha build, came a new layout. In previous builds our academy felt rather empty and scattered. Larger isn’t always better, so we reworked the academy size and building placements around for a more compact look. There are some drawbacks to this approach, mainly less natural environmental elements such as lakes, trees, and waterfalls. Instead, we compensate by providing more space for player decorations and customization. Thankfully, testers appreciated the change, complimenting the academy’s more fitting décor and the overall compact layout.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/74ebd7490ad9407d9c1cf52caac1bcab74b39919.png[/img]

5.	Visual Improvements

As the game progress we continue to improve on its overall appearance. Adding more 2d illustrations, 3d models, effects, and visual novel aspects to the game, making the game livelier and more visually appealing for our testers. Here’s a sneak peek of our updates below! Do note that we will continue to refine the game visuals, and what you see currently might be changed in the final product.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/7ece86a52fc0a8a739271953de3f3d7972ce2f1a.png[/img]

6.	UI/UX Update

More than 60% of testers admire the UI’s visual appeal, but some were still confused with the UI’s clarity. As a result, we’ve modified the UI for better readability, and provided more informative displays such as building lists and student information. We also managed to fix most of the previous build’s UI bugs and hope our efforts show good results in the 5th Alpha test. 
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/1728f94d20e1fa34fae7ee24b8bf4f8c89655022.png[/img]

Overall, playtesting has gone quite smoothly and it’s all thanks to all you early principals who joined our playtests! We owe it to you guys for noticing our shortcomings and giving us your input to make VAHSS2 the best it can be!

If you’re interested in becoming a play tester for the 5th alpha build, come register here: https://bit.ly/alphateststeam. Your input is very valuable to us and is always appreciated. Well, that’s all from us for now.

notes.title: Dev Diary #4: Students' Majoring System
notes.notes:
Greetings, Principals! Welcome back to our beloved Dev Diary series!  
 

After a thorough explanation about our academy and how it works for our students, it’s finally time to talk about the students themselves. As we have mentioned in our previous diary, students will have proficiencies depending on which major they’re assigned to. Thus, in this diary we’re going to point out all the different majors and their advantages. 

To start, we want to remind you that in HSS2, we will be calling classes as majors. Essentially, they’re the same. However, like in any other academy, there are classrooms, so we decided to avoid the headache and differentiate the two. So, Knights, Mages, and others, are considered as majors in HSS2.  

There will be 4 proficiencies in HSS2, each of those proficiencies belong to 4 different Base Majors. Base Majors are the ones students have with them when they first enroll the academy. They come with 1 proficiency that can break 1 of the enemy’s shield. with the same proficiency.  

The Base Majors are:  

[olist]
[*] Knight with Physical proficiency. 
[*] Magi with Magic proficiency.
[*] Cleric with Divine proficiency.  
[*] Arcsmith with Arc proficiency.  
[/olist]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/3ed4c85af7c37f47ff3039118b421cb087e9321b.png[/img]
Image of base major student in Blender

As your students progress, more majors will become available, such as the Mixed and Advanced Majors. Currently there are 6 Mixed Majors and 4 Advanced Majors available. Mixed Majors have 2 proficiencies and are able to break 1 shield per hit.  

The Mixed Majors are:  

[olist]
[*] Ksatria with Physical / Magic proficiencies. 
[*] Scholarsage with Magic / Divine proficiencies.  
[*] Bogatyr with Physical / Divine proficiencies. 
[*] Arc Draconus with Physical / Arc proficiencies.  
[*] Arc Magica with Physical / Magic proficiencies.  
[*] Arc Divina with Physical / Divine proficiencies.  
[/olist]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/ff9501bd2f06e2ea395b39621bd89f8c03c5d47b.png[/img]
Image of mix major student, testing in Unreal Engine

Mixed Majors have 2 different proficiencies. Meanwhile, Advanced Majors have 2 of the same proficiency and are able to break 2 shields per hit.  

The Advanced Majors are: 

[olist]
[*] Paladin with 2 Physical proficiencies. 
[*] Summoner with 2 Magic proficiencies. 
[*] Medica with 2 Divine proficiencies. 
[*] Architech with 2 Arc proficiencies. 
[/olist]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/7ece86a52fc0a8a739271953de3f3d7972ce2f1a.png[/img]
Image of advance major student, testing in Blender

Players can decide which major the students will change to. Changing majors is possible after the selected student have taken the necessary courses connected to the major’s requirements. For example, if the player wants their student to change into a Paladin, the student has to clear the course “Physical Training III.” After passing the course, the student will have the ability to change into their new major on these designated times: 

[olist]
[*] During exams which occurs once every 6 months. 
[*] Player directed, outside of exams. (limited) 
[/olist]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/af732e6543b5b35140d3c46bbc30067ee7396a74.png[/img]
Image of promoting student (not final product)

We hope the major changing system provides more dynamic gameplay and a chance to experiment with different majors. It should also give players more flexibility, as even newly enrolled students with lower stats can be of help to senior students simply because they have the right proficiencies. A good principal pay attention to all their students abilities and improve their skills accordingly. 

However, like any other update and improvements we brought to the game, we are uncertain whether this system would bring the experience we intended. We also have concerns whether allowing to change majors will drive players to change majors repeatedly instead of maximizing their students true potential.  

Still, that’s for us to fuss about, you guys just sit back, relax, and enjoy the game! That’s all for today’s dev diary, thanks for sticking around until the end. Hope to see you in the next one, Principals!

notes.title: Dev Diary #3: First Look at The Academy
notes.notes:
Greetings, Principal! Welcome back to our Dev Diary series.  

After describing in detail about the new combat system in Hero School Story 2, this diary will cover the beginning of the academy section of the series. The academy is, of course, the place where you, as the principal, shape the students to grow and be ready for combat, by providing the best environment to help them reach their maximum potential. In this diary, we are going to explain about the new aspects that did not exist and improvements made from the prequel.  
 

Based on the player feedback we got from HSS, many players felt that the real time progression is too slow and felt too long to progress. So, in HSS2, we wanted to introduce a new feature called “Skip Time'' which allows players to be able to freely progress. This feature makes it easier to adjust the playstyle of each principal. (See pic)  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/8a3d37fa425d099c40587e533cf14cb53ed2ff07.png[/img]
 

We would like to mention that in HSS there are random events in the form of cutscenes that can occur inside the academy: students are late for class or even missing their wallet. However, there is not much you can do from these random events. So, we decided to spice it up in HSS2, by doubling down on random events which then players can react to and students will respond according to their personality. We plan to make the events affect the students, though we will describe it further at a later date.   
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/e06af1c9d31ea72a15deb3946e24fb5297a563a8.png[/img]

We plan to add personalities for the students in the academy. Their personality will vary from one student to another, so the academy will feel a little more realistic. We plan to cover this in more details on the next diaries, and we hope that players can enjoy the new and improved version of the random events brought to HSS2. 
 

The academy improvements do not stop there. Buildings are also a huge part of the academy that plays an important part in the students’ growth. In HSS2, buildings are now simplified and are all the same size, which are then classified into 2 types, Classes and Facilities. Players have the freedom to choose between the two according to their needs, classes give more flexibility as only selected students get the benefits from the selected class, while Facilities carry overall buff to all the students in the academy.  


For example, if there are 3 free slots of building, you can build either all 3 classes or 1 class plus 2 facilities, etc. The choice is freely decided by how you want to improve your students! Adding 3 classes will make it easier for you to choose between assigning which students go to class A, B, or C. Adding more facilities means you will grant your academy plenty of permanent stat buffs for the rest of the game. 

After mentioning students’ personalities, random events and buildings that exist in the academy, we will now talk about time and how it works in the academy of HSS2. Back in the prequel, whenever the graduation pop up appears, principals are required to put one or more students to graduate, regardless of their academic achievements. In HSS2, students will always graduate after 3 years in the academy. 1 year consists of 4 seasons and 1 season consists of 3 months to which then the players can assign students to the classes every month. At the end of each season, principals can send their students into combat. This is a major difference between HSS1 and HSS2, where in HSS1 players can send students into combat anytime, but in HSS2, players will have to prioritize their choices in order to improve the students’ potential.  
 

With this many improvements and changes in HSS2, we hope players will enjoy their time building the best academy in Valthiria with the new concept. We now wrap up the academy briefing for all the principals that are excited to start their academy soon.  

Thank you for your time reading, and please don’t forget to wishlist us!

notes.title: Dev Diary #2: Elements of Battle
notes.notes:
Welcome back to our Dev Diary series, Principal!

This time we would like to specifically talk about our newest battle system called Shield Break mentioned in our previous dev diary. Explaining in detail about how Shield Break would work for our students in combat.

To start it off, we must introduce a new feature in HSS2 called “Proficiency”. Proficiencies are used in two ways. On enemies, it is presented in a sequence that determines their “Shield”. On students, it is a property of their current class. In simple terms, it’s akin to a ”weapon type” that can “Break” the enemies’ Shield of the same type. 

There are 4 different proficiencies that principals have to pay attention to. (See pic below)
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/6506fcfac6e7d94f99c0c68d8620b3952549f0b2.png[/img]
 
Breaking enemies shield gives various tide-turning benefits, such as the ability to deal massive damage or resetting their attack cooldown. All student classes have Proficiency, even low-level ones, so that when Principals bring them along into combat they can serve a function instead of just being a burden. With this Shield Break system, we’re hoping to see Principals utilize a wide range of student rosters in battle for different circumstances instead of having a “favorite team” to fall back into every time. 

To further explain the Shield Break system, let’s use this next picture as an example: 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/771efec95faaa3efb8a951e3e7e57d1d107244d4.png[/img] 

The enemies in the picture have a different set of proficiencies that our students have to break in order to deal extra damage:
[list]
[*] Enemy A has a Shield with MM sequence 
[*] Enemy B has a Shield with PPD sequence
[/list]
In order for the students to benefit from Shield Break, Enemy A has to be attacked in the correct sequence:
[list]
[*] Two hits from a Magic-proficiency student
[/list]
And Enemy B has to be attacked in this exact sequence:
[list]
[*]  Two hits from a Physical-proficiency student
[*]  One hit from a Divine-proficiency student
[/list]
After breaking the Shield, the enemy will have sign that shows “Shield Break”. Any students that deal damage will benefit from it no matter the Proficiency they have. 

Despite its importance, Shield Breaking is not mandatory. Even when an enemy’s Shield isn’t broken, students will still be able to deal damage, albeit at a reduced rate. So if you don’t bring the optimal roster into battle, or don’t have the right students in your academy, you’ll still be able to get through combat with a some more effort.

With this new information explained, we hope that principals would get the idea and be as excited as us while developing this new system! 

We now will wrap up the diary Number 2 that explains how Shield Break works and we will see you in our next diary. Thank you for your time reading!

notes.title: Dev Diary #1: New Battle System
notes.notes:
Greetings, Principal!

As we have mentioned in our previous diary, this time we would like to give you a more in-depth explanation about our new combat system in this sequel. In HSS, the game combat system is based on its fast-paced, action-based system and now in HSS2 it has become a fast-paced, turn-based system. By changing the combat system, we hope it would provide more comprehensive gameplay for all our players.

We should start by mentioning on what we learn from Hero School Story. Based on player feedback on HSS, there was a conflict between the fast-paced combat and the slower-paced academy. A significant portion of players liked one thing but not so much the other. Additionally, in HSS, the combat was heavily influenced by players' dexterity and mechanical skills, and therefore the students' progression in the academy didn't matter much in combat. (see pic below)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/44f33ce756ec2cface960fa04603cb9f50d6f7bb.png[/img]

So, in HSS2, we decided to rework the combat into a turn-based system. This will require strategic thinking and be more consistent with the academy management section. The idea is to reward players who properly prepared their students in the academy before going into battle, and every bit of progress made by the students can be immediately felt in combat.

Combat in HSS2 introduces a "Shield Break" system, in which you have to match student proficiencies with enemies' defenses. This encourages not only bringing a higher variety of students into battle compared to HSS, but it also challenges the player to develop a diverse roster in their academy (or focus in specific proficiencies). (pic below)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40306402/d2c2ddaf1f1a4a9a5d88013c9ae4d88b4b84d61d.png[/img]

We realize that the game has taken quite a turn in terms of its combat experience for players from the previous game (HSS1). However, we are sure that players old or new would be able to enjoy the more comprehensive combat system that we introduce in HSS2. With this we wrap up the Number 1 diary and there will be more to come to update you all on what we are working on for our beloved academy. 

Thank you for your time reading!

notes.title: Dev Diary #0: Introduction
notes.notes:
Greetings, Principal!

Welcome to our Dev Diary series where we’ll update regularly about what we’re doing, what we’re changing... or just the development in general! In this series, you’ll be given a detailed information regarding Valthirian Arc: Hero School Story 2’s development.

To kick it off, we’d like to highlight the notable changes in Hero School Story 2 compared to the first one, and we’ll give you more in-depth explanation of the changes (and additional features) in the future Dev Diaries.

[list]
[*][b]Combat System[/b]
From what you might’ve guessed from the shots on our page, HSS2 now uses a turn-based system instead of action-based like the previous game. Previously, the combat felt a bit too simple, so we decided to spice it up and make it more interesting by whipping up a turn-based system for this game. It will still be fast-paced like before, so it can provide a break from the slow-thinking academy, but it still reward those who play it smart.

[*][b]Academy[/b]
In HSS, we noticed that players tend to spend the majority of their time casually smacking monsters, which isn’t what we intended the game to be about (it’s a school sim game first and foremost). Therefore, we’re trying to balance between the combat and academy management by 50-50 each, to actually make you feel like a principal in your own academy. Moreover, we will deliver better principal experiences for players by developing a better interaction with their student.

[*][b]Art[/b]
We are extremely thankful that you loved the art design in HSS, though there were mentions of how the environment somehow made it look like a mobile game. In this sequel, we wanted to keep the cuteness along with the depth from each character but simpler than HSS, while improving the quality of the art and bring it to the next level. 

[*][b]Narrative[/b]
We’d also like to tell you that in HSS2, you’ll be able to explore more on the story! From the characters and main quests, we aim to make a better storyline than HSS. There will be multiple plots, character stories, and also a different, and more interesting plot from the prequel. You’ll also see some familiar faces in HSS2! So you can feel nostalgic throughout your playthrough.
[/list]
We know that some of these changes will be far more different than the previous titles, but hopefully it will create a new and better experience in playing Valthirian Arc series. We’ll reveal more of our game and the development in the following diaries. Wishlist us and stay tuned for more!
